evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.106: est modus in rēbus
Plaut. Poen. 238: modus omnibus rēbus … optimus est habitū
terms.comment: To set a limit: modum facere with the genitive (inimīcitiārum modum facere, Cic. Sull. 48, Lewis & Short) or modum statuere with the dative (cupidinibus statuat nātūra modum, Hor. S. 1.2.111); without limit, sine modō.

evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.106: sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
terms.comment: Also the end of something (see end).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.70: nūllīs ut terminīs circumscrībat aut dēfīniat jūs suum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Tusc. 1.62: paucīs litterārum notīs termināvit
Cic. Mil. 88: senātus, crēdō, praetōrem eum circumscrīpsisset

phrases.latin: est modus in rēbus, sunt certī dēnique fīnēs
phrases.english: there is a measure in things; there are, in short, fixed limits

phrases.latin: modus omnibus rēbus, soror, optimus est habitū
phrases.english: keeping within limits, sister, is best in everything

phrases.latin: quī sonōs vōcis, quī īnfīnītī vidēbantur, paucīs litterārum notīs termināvit
phrases.english: the man who confined the sounds of the voice, which seemed limitless, to a few letters
